narrative.overview: A well-kept ledger on a daylit desk: quiet, ruled, trustworthy, and easy to read for hours. Rows are the primary object; chrome recedes; every state is written down in words rather than implied by colour. It replaces a dense spreadsheet-style skin with 14px text, 36px controls, 56px rows, horizontal rules only, and every text pairing measured at 5.5:1 or better.
keyCharacteristics: One cool neutral family (hue 262) and one navy accent used only for primary action, selection and focus.
Status always travels with a word plus a dot or icon.
Mono type is reserved for identifiers and measurements.
Permissions are visible: unusable controls stay, disabled, with the rule beside them.
Restrained motion: sheets slide in, changed rows settle from a tint, nothing else animates.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Navy is for the thing you can do next and the thing that is selected. It never decorates, never colours a heading, and never fills a status.

rules.name: The Words Beside Colour Rule
rules.body: Every status tint is paired with its word and a dot or icon. A greyscale screenshot must still say Assigned, In storage, Retired, Poor.

rules.name: The Measured Grey Rule
rules.body: Text greys are chosen from measured contrast, not by eye. Nothing carrying meaning goes below 4.5:1; ink-4 is decoration only.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: If it is an identifier, a timestamp or a measured value, it is mono and tabular. If it is a sentence or a label, it is Geist.

rules.name: The Twelve Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No text under 12px. Anything that matters is 14px.

rules.name: The Blur Has an Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has a y or x offset and a soft blur. No zero-offset glows, no hard block shadows.

rules.name: The Floating Means Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it does not float above the page, it has no pop shadow.

dos: Do keep text at 14px for anything a person reads or scans, 12px for metadata only, and every meaningful text pair at 4.5:1 or better.
Do give every status a word plus a dot or icon, and every disabled rule a visible reason.
Do set identifiers, timestamps and counts in Geist Mono or tabular figures so columns align.
Do keep controls at 36px (32px inside rows) and rows at 56px; make the common path keyboard-complete.
Do open focused tasks in the right-hand sheet and save centred dialogs for confirmations.
Do self-host fonts and icons. The app must work on a network with no internet.
donts: Don't return to the spec's spreadsheet skin: no borders on every cell, no 9.5-11px labels, no controls under 32px, no greys under 4.5:1 for text.
Don't build the overview from a grid of same-size KPI cards or hero numbers; lead with what needs a decision.
Don't use the accent for decoration, headings or status fills.
Don't use a coloured side stripe on rows, cards or alerts. The row highlight is a tint, not a bar.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons (keyboard hints included); use the Lucide set.
Don't put a mono face on labels or sentences, or a display face on UI text.
Don't hide a control the user may not use. Disable it and say why.
Don't add motion beyond sheet entry, menu pop-ins and the row settle, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
